execution.checkpointing.interval.desc: Sets the time interval for execution checkpoints in milliseconds. This parameter is used to enable and control the frequency of state snapshots, which can alleviate disk IO bottlenecks during system state recovery. Increasing this value reduces checkpoint frequency, thereby lowering system load, but may increase recovery time; decreasing this value improves data consistency but increases system load. To enable checkpoints, this value must be set to a positive integer greater than 0

execution.checkpointing.max-concurrent-c.desc: Sets the maximum number of concurrent checkpoints to control the number of simultaneous checkpoints. Increasing this value improves system concurrency but may cause resource competition; decreasing this value reduces system load but may affect data consistency. This parameter can alleviate potential disk IO bottlenecks during the checkpoint process

execution.checkpointing.min-pause.desc: Sets the minimum pause time between two consecutive checkpoints in milliseconds. This parameter controls the interval between checkpoints and can alleviate potential CPU bottlenecks during the checkpoint process. Increasing this value reduces checkpoint frequency and lowers system load; decreasing this value increases checkpoint frequency but may cause system resource competition

execution.checkpointing.timeout.desc: Sets the timeout for checkpoints in milliseconds; used to control the maximum execution time of checkpoints, which can alleviate potential memory bottlenecks during the checkpoint process. Increasing this value tolerates longer checkpoint times but may increase system resource usage; decreasing this value speeds up failure detection but may cause frequent checkpoint failures

jobmanager.memory.jvm-overhead.max.desc: Sets the maximum overhead memory for JobManager JVM to ensure sufficient memory for JVM under high load. Increasing this value can alleviate memory bottlenecks and improve system stability. This parameter specifies non-heap memory reserved for JVM overhead, such as thread stack space, compilation cache, etc

jobmanager.memory.jvm-overhead.min.desc: Sets the minimum overhead memory for JobManager JVM to ensure sufficient memory for JVM operation. This parameter reserves non-heap memory overhead for JVM, including thread stack space, compilation cache, etc. Increasing this value can alleviate memory bottlenecks and avoid frequent garbage collection by JVM

parallelism.default.desc: Sets the default parallelism for Flink jobs; if parallelism is not specified, this value is used. Increasing this value can alleviate CPU bottlenecks and improve job execution efficiency. Default value is 1, maximum value is 128

restart-strategy.fixed-delay.attempts.desc: Sets the number of restart attempts for fixed delay restart strategy; used to control the number of restarts when tasks fail, which can alleviate CPU bottlenecks during system failure recovery. Increasing this value improves task recovery capability but may increase resource usage; decreasing this value speeds up failure detection but may cause task loss

restart-strategy.fixed-delay.delay.desc: This parameter sets the restart delay time for fixed delay restart strategy in milliseconds. It controls the restart wait time after task failure and can alleviate network bottlenecks during system failure recovery. Increasing this value reduces restart frequency and lowers system load; decreasing this value speeds up restart but may cause resource competition

restart-strategy.desc: Defines the restart strategy when tasks fail to alleviate memory bottlenecks during system failure recovery. Optional values include: 'none' (no restart), 'fixed-delay' (fixed delay restart), 'failure-rate' (failure rate based restart), 'exponential-delay' (exponential delay restart)

state.backend.incremental.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable incremental snapshots, controlling the storage method of state snapshots. Enabling incremental snapshots reduces storage space usage and alleviates disk IO bottlenecks during state management, but may increase recovery time

state.backend.desc: Sets the state backend type; defines how Flink stores state, which can alleviate disk IO bottlenecks during state management. Optional values include 'memory', 'filesystem', and 'rocksdb'

state.backend.rocksdb.block.cache-size.desc: Sets the block cache size for RocksDB in bytes. This parameter controls the number of data blocks cached in memory by RocksDB, thereby improving read performance

state.backend.rocksdb.checkpoint.transfe.desc: This parameter sets the number of threads per stateful operator used for transferring (downloading and uploading) RocksDBStateBackend files

state.backend.rocksdb.compaction.level.m.desc: Sets the maximum compaction level base size for RocksDB in bytes. This parameter optimizes storage performance and can alleviate disk I/O bottlenecks during state management

state.backend.rocksdb.thread.num.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of concurrent background flush and compaction jobs for RocksDB (per stateful operator)

state.backend.rocksdb.use-bloom-filter.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable Bloom Filter to optimize RocksDB query performance

state.backend.rocksdb.write-batch-size.desc: Sets the write batch size for RocksDB in bytes. This parameter optimizes write performance

state.backend.rocksdb.writebuffer.count.desc: Sets the number of write buffers for RocksDB to optimize write performance

taskmanager.numberOfTaskSlots.desc: This parameter sets the number of task slots for TaskManager, determining the number of tasks that a single TaskManager can process in parallel

jobmanager.memory.process.size.desc: Total memory size of the JobManager process. Includes JVM heap memory, non-heap memory (direct memory, native memory), JVM metaspace, and JVM overhead. In containerized environments, should be set to the container memory size

jobmanager.memory.jvm-metaspace.size.desc: JVM metaspace size for the JobManager. Default value is 256 MB

taskmanager.memory.process.size.desc: Total memory size of the TaskManager process. Includes total Flink memory, JVM metaspace, and JVM overhead. In containerized environments, should be set to the container memory size

taskmanager.memory.jvm-metaspace.size.desc: JVM metaspace size for the TaskManager. Default value is 256 MB

taskmanager.memory.framework.heap.size.desc: JVM heap memory size used by the TaskManager framework. This memory is not allocated to task slots

taskmanager.memory.framework.off-heap.ba.desc: Memory size for reading shuffle data in batch shuffle (sort-merge shuffle). This memory is allocated from `taskmanager.memory.framework.off-heap.size`

taskmanager.memory.jvm-overhead.fraction.desc: Proportion of total process memory reserved for JVM overhead (e.g., thread stacks, compilation cache). Default value is 0.1

taskmanager.memory.jvm-overhead.max.desc: Maximum size of TaskManager JVM overhead. Default value is 1 GB

taskmanager.memory.jvm-overhead.min.desc: Minimum size of TaskManager JVM overhead. Default value is 192 MB

taskmanager.memory.network.fraction.desc: Proportion of network memory to total Flink memory. Network memory is non-heap memory reserved for the ShuffleEnvironment (e.g., network buffers). Default value is 0.1

taskmanager.memory.network.min.desc: Minimum network memory size for TaskManager. Default value is 64 MB

taskmanager.memory.network.max.desc: Maximum network memory size for the TaskManager. Network memory is non-heap memory reserved for the ShuffleEnvironment (e.g., network buffers). Default value is 1 GB

taskmanager.network.numberOfBuffers.desc: Number of buffers used by the TaskManager for network transmission. This value determines the amount of direct memory the TaskManager can use for network data exchange. The default value depends on the TaskManager's memory settings

taskmanager.network.memory.buffers-per-c.desc: Number of dedicated buffers allocated per outgoing/incoming channel. Used to reduce data contention

taskmanager.network.memory.floating-buff.desc: Number of floating buffers allocated per input gate. These buffers are shared among multiple channels to handle data skew

taskmanager.network.memory.max-buffers-p.desc: Maximum number of buffers that can be allocated per channel

taskmanager.network.blocking-shuffle.typ.desc: Type of blocking shuffle implementation used by TaskManager for batch jobs. 'file': uses file storage for shuffle data; 'mmap': uses memory-mapped files

taskmanager.network.blocking-shuffle.com.desc: Whether to enable compression for blocking shuffle data. Compression reduces network and disk I/O but increases CPU load

taskmanager.network.sort-shuffle.min-buf.desc: Minimum number of network buffers required for Sort Shuffle

taskmanager.network.sort-shuffle.min-par.desc: Minimum parallelism to trigger Sort Shuffle. When job parallelism is below this value, other shuffle implementations may be used

taskmanager.network.request-backoff.init.desc: Initial backoff time (milliseconds) after a network request failure. When the peer is unavailable, the TaskManager will wait this long before retrying the network request

taskmanager.network.request-backoff.max.desc: Maximum backoff time (milliseconds) after a network request failure. Retry intervals will increase exponentially until reaching this maximum

taskmanager.runtime.hashjoin-bloom-filte.desc: Whether to use Bloom Filters in Hash Join operations. Bloom filters can filter out non-matching join keys in advance, reducing processing load

taskmanager.runtime.max-fan.desc: Maximum fan-out number when merging partitions in batch operations. For example, in sort-merge join, this controls the number of source partitions a single partition can merge

taskmanager.runtime.sort-spilling-thresh.desc: Threshold (ratio of sort memory) at which sorting data begins to be spilled to disk during sort operations. Lower values cause more frequent spilling and less memory usage

taskmanager.runtime.large-record-handler.desc: Whether to enable the Large Record handler for processing oversized records that exceed network buffer size

akka.throughput.desc: Maximum throughput of messages processed by a single Actor in Akka remoting. This value determines the maximum number of messages an Actor can process before yielding control to the thread pool

akka.fork-join-executor.parallelism-max.desc: Maximum parallelism of the Akka fork-join thread pool. Affects the concurrency capability of Akka message processing

heartbeat.interval.desc: Interval (milliseconds) at which heartbeats are sent between JobManager and TaskManager to detect whether components are alive

blob.fetch.backlog.desc: Maximum queue size of pending BLOB fetch requests in the Blob service. BLOB (Binary Large Object) is used to distribute large files (e.g., JAR files) between JobManager and TaskManager

blob.fetch.num-concurrent.desc: Maximum number of concurrent BLOB fetch operations allowed in the Blob service

state.checkpoints.num-retained.desc: Maximum number of completed Checkpoints to retain. When this number is exceeded, the oldest Checkpoint will be deleted. Default value is 1

execution.checkpointing.mode.desc: Checkpoint mode. 'EXACTLY_ONCE': exactly-once semantics; 'AT_LEAST_ONCE': at-least-once semantics

execution.checkpointing.prefer-checkpoin.desc: Whether to prefer Checkpoints over Savepoints for recovery. If `true` and a Checkpoint exists, it will be used preferentially

execution.checkpointing.unaligned.desc: Whether to enable Unaligned Checkpoints. When enabled, Checkpoint speed can be faster under backpressure, but increases I/O load

execution.checkpointing.unaligned.forced.desc: Whether to force the use of Unaligned Checkpoints for all Checkpoints. If enabled, other conditions are ignored

execution.checkpointing.snapshot-compres.desc: Whether to compress Checkpoint snapshot data. Enabling this reduces snapshot size but increases CPU load

state.storage.fs.memory-threshold.desc: Minimum size threshold (KB) for state data to be written to a file in the filesystem state storage. State smaller than this threshold will be stored as metadata in JobManager memory

state.storage.fs.write-buffer-size.desc: Write buffer size (bytes) used by the filesystem state storage when writing Checkpoint data

state.backend.rocksdb.memory.managed.desc: Whether the RocksDB state backend uses Flink managed memory. If `true`, RocksDB automatically uses the Slot's managed memory budget

state.backend.rocksdb.memory.partitioned.desc: Whether to use partitioned indexes/filters. Partitioning can split index and filter blocks into smaller sub-blocks and load them into memory only when needed, reducing memory usage

state.backend.rocksdb.memory.write-buffe.desc: Maximum memory ratio for write buffers, based on the total shared memory managed by RocksDB. The remaining memory is used for block cache. Default value is 0.5

state.backend.rocksdb.memory.high-prio-p.desc: Proportion of cache memory reserved for high-priority data (e.g., indexes, filters, compression dictionary blocks). Default value is 0.1

state.backend.rocksdb.writebuffer.size.desc: Size of a single write buffer (in MB). Write buffers are memory pools for RocksDB memtables

state.backend.rocksdb.writebuffer.number.desc: Number of memtables that can be merged before flushing to disk

state.backend.rocksdb.block.blocksize.desc: Size of SST file blocks in RocksDB (in KB). Larger blocks can improve sequential read performance but reduce point lookup efficiency. Default value is 4KB

state.backend.rocksdb.block.metadata-blo.desc: Size of blocks storing metadata in RocksDB (in KB). Default value is 4KB

state.backend.rocksdb.bloom-filter.block.desc: Whether to enable a specific optimization mode for block-based Bloom Filters. Bloom filters are used to speed up key lookups

state.backend.rocksdb.bloom-filter.bits-.desc: Number of bits allocated per key in the Bloom Filter. Higher values reduce false positive rates but consume more memory. Default value is 10.0

state.backend.rocksdb.compaction.style.desc: Compaction strategy for RocksDB. 'LEVEL': Leveled Compaction (default); 'UNIVERSAL': Universal Compaction, suitable for write-intensive workloads; 'FIFO': FIFO Compaction, for temporary data; 'NONE': no Compaction

state.backend.rocksdb.compaction.level.t.desc: Target size (in MB) for each SST file in RocksDB Level-1. Larger values reduce the number of files but may increase Compaction overhead

state.backend.rocksdb.compaction.level.u.desc: Whether to use dynamic target sizes to control file sizes across RocksDB levels. When enabled, sizes can be adjusted dynamically based on actual conditions

state.backend.rocksdb.predefined-options.desc: Predefined optimization configuration sets for RocksDB. Choose the appropriate configuration based on the underlying storage medium. 'DEFAULT': default settings; 'SPINNING_DISK_OPTIMIZED': optimization for HDD; 'FLASH_SSD_OPTIMIZED': optimization for SSD

pipeline.max-parallelism.desc: Default maximum parallelism for the entire pipeline. This value affects the number of state partitions for KeyedStreams

pipeline.operator-chaining.desc: Whether to enable Operator Chaining optimization. When disabled, each operator runs in an independent task
